section_summary: This section traces postwar efforts to relieve food, clothing, medical, and welfare shortages in occupied Japan, beginning with proposals from Japanese communities in Brazil and petitions from Chinese residents of western Japan. It documents the gradual establishment of approved private-relief channels—especially the Licensed Agencies for Relief in Asia (LARA)—alongside requests for social-work training materials and debates over Japanese food policy, relief appropriations, and the use of Japanese liquid assets. Later records concern relief offers from Argentina and Chile, assistance for Okinawa, and Chinese medical supplies donated to victims of the December 1946 Shikoku earthquake.

keywords: Licensed Agencies for Relief in Asia (LARA)
Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)

subfiles.title: Japanese Colony in São Paulo Proposal for Relief Shipments to Japan
subfiles.from: American Consulate General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Reports a proposal by Japanese residents of São Paulo to contribute money, food, and clothing for relief in Japan and requests guidance.
subfiles.summary: Sao Paulo's Japanese community asks to send relief to Japan, possibly a steamer monthly, with Kiyoshi Yamamoto and Shigetsuma Furuya promoting; the airgram asks about using the Red Cross and urges sending Japanese newspapers to counter reports that Japan wasn't defeated.

subfiles.title: Reply Concerning the São Paulo Japanese Relief Proposal
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Advises that the relief proposal has been referred to the occupation authorities in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: State says the Sao Paulo proposal went to the Acting Political Adviser to SCAP, and an inquiry was made about getting current Japanese newspapers for Brazil.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to SCAP on Brazilian Relief Shipments and Japanese Newspapers
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo, for George Atcheson Jr.
subfiles.about: Requests clarification of occupation policy governing relief shipments from Brazil and asks for Japanese newspapers.
subfiles.summary: State asks SCAP whether food and clothing offered by Brazil's Japanese community may enter occupied Japan and by what approval, and endorses the consulate's request for newspapers to convince skeptics Japan was defeated; page 5 is a mail-section routing sheet.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Chinese Residents' Petition
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Walter S. Robertson, American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Chungking
subfiles.about: Forwards a Chinese residents' petition for preferential relief treatment in western Japan.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson encloses a memorandum and a November 16 petition from Chinese residents of western Japan seeking special treatment, suggesting the Embassy discreetly inform China while omitting the Political Adviser's comments.

subfiles.title: Request of Chinese Residents for Preferential Treatment
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander and Chief of Staff
subfiles.about: Comments on a petition from long-term Chinese residents of the Kansai region.
subfiles.summary: Memo: the petitioners are mainly long-term Chinese business residents, not prisoners or forced laborers, many perhaps accommodated to the Wang Ching-wei regime; no recommendation, with repatriation possibly resolving much of the problem.

subfiles.title: Petition of the Overseas Chinese in the Kansai District
subfiles.from: Li Wan-shih and Pan To-yuen, Delegation of Overseas Chinese in the Kansai District
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests food, housing, clothing, communications, education, and repatriation assistance for Chinese residents of western Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kansai's 5,533 Chinese and about 20,000 Formosans, many in barracks, complain of poor rations, frozen deposits, no clothing or bedding, banned communications and destroyed schools, and ask equal foreign-national rations, more rice and help returning to China.

subfiles.title: Woman's Association Appeal for Relief to Defeated Countries
subfiles.from: Mildred Waitt, Woman's Association, First Congregational Church of Portland
subfiles.about: Urges that Japan, Germany, and other defeated countries be opened to shipments of food.
subfiles.summary: A Portland church women's association telegraphs it voted to advocate admitting food shipments to defeated countries, naming Japan and Germany.

subfiles.title: Note on Purchasing Far Eastern Rubber
subfiles.about: Records notification that the United States would purchase allocated natural Far Eastern rubber at a stated price.
subfiles.summary: Note on buying top-grade Far Eastern rubber allocated to the U.S. at 20 1/4 pence per pound, apparently interfiled by mistake.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mildred Waitt on Relief for Japan and Germany
subfiles.from: Eldred D. Kuppinger for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains the current policies governing private food relief for Japan and Germany.
subfiles.summary: State tells Mildred Waitt imports into Japan could be approved if occupation authorities deem them necessary for a minimum living standard, with private-relief policy pending; private aid to Germany was acceptable in principle but awaited distribution arrangements and War Relief Control Board registration.

subfiles.title: Inquiry About Christian Science Relief Supplies for Japan
subfiles.from: James Brunot, President's War Relief Control Board
subfiles.to: Eldred D. Kuppinger, Department of State
subfiles.about: Asks whether circumstances permit Christian Science relief supplies to be sent to an Army chaplain in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Brunot says the Christian Science War Relief Committee wanted to supply needy Christian Scientists in Japan through an Army chaplain; the Board declined for lack of a channel, military needs coverage and the Trading with the Enemy Act, and he asks whether anything changed.

subfiles.title: Reply to James Brunot on Relief Shipments
subfiles.from: Eldred D. Kuppinger, Department of State
subfiles.to: James Brunot, President's War Relief Control Board
subfiles.about: Confirms that there is no new information permitting relief shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kuppinger tells Brunot nothing can yet be added; Tokyo was queried late in 1945 without reply, and he'll pass along any information.

subfiles.title: CINCAFPAC Cable on a System for Private Japanese Relief
subfiles.from: CINCAFPAC, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Recommends collecting private relief supplies at a single point for bulk shipment and international distribution in Japan.
subfiles.summary: CINCAFPAC: offers of food and clothing are welcome, but small individual shipments are hard to handle; it recommends consolidated bulk shipments distributed by an international organization like the Red Cross, addressing Brazil's Japanese community proposal.

subfiles.title: Instruction to São Paulo Holding Relief Shipments in Abeyance
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Reports that private relief would be welcomed but must await an approved handling and distribution policy.
subfiles.summary: State tells Sao Paulo occupation authorities welcome private relief in principle, but without handling and distribution procedures its shipments stay in abeyance.

subfiles.title: Memorandum Urging Development of Private-Relief Procedures
subfiles.from: Division of Japanese Affairs
subfiles.about: Urges consultation on a method for forwarding and distributing private relief supplies in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Memo urges a workable procedure for private contributions as American tradition and recommends consulting Mr. Whitman and others who had considered it.

subfiles.title: Proposal for a Coordinated Private-Relief Channel to Japan
subfiles.from: Special Projects Division, signed Albert E. Clattenburg
subfiles.about: Proposes coordinated collection, shipping, and distribution arrangements for private relief to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Memo proposes a coordinated relief channel: a West Coast port, a War Relief Control Board-approved agency, Army shipping and distribution by the Red Cross or a model like occupied Germany's, approaching the War Department's Civil Affairs Division.
keywords: International Committee of the Red Cross

subfiles.title: Copy of CINCAFPAC Cable CA 57974
subfiles.from: CINCAFPAC, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Restates the recommendation for consolidated private-relief shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Copy of CINCAFPAC cable CA 57974 of February 17: welcomes food and clothing, warns against uncoordinated small shipments, favors one collection point, bulk transport and distribution by the Red Cross.

subfiles.title: Nominees for the Voluntary-Agencies Mission to Japan
subfiles.from: Fred Atkins Moore and Charlotte E. Owen, American Council of Voluntary Agencies for Foreign Service
subfiles.about: Requests urgent travel clearance for five proposed members of a relief-planning mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Council nominates Edward McMahon, Esther Rhoads, Leland Brubaker, G. Ernest Bott and Michael McKillop for a voluntary-agencies mission to Japan to coordinate with Military Government and recommend relief services, and asks immediate State clearance.

subfiles.title: Member Agencies of the American Council of Voluntary Agencies
subfiles.from: American Council of Voluntary Agencies for Foreign Service
subfiles.about: Lists the relief, refugee, religious, labor, and social-service organizations belonging to the Council.
subfiles.summary: Printed roster of the American Council of Voluntary Agencies' member and associate agencies.

subfiles.title: Reply on the Modified Voluntary-Agencies Mission
subfiles.from: Willard L. Thorp, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains that the proposed five-person mission had been revised to a three-person study group pending General MacArthur's approval.
subfiles.summary: Thorp notes later conferences among the Council, War Department and War Relief Control Board; the revised plan has three members, one already in Japan, examining relief on terms acceptable to SCAP, and Moore will be notified after Tokyo responds.

subfiles.title: Bombay Telegram on Press Reports of Japanese Food Conditions
subfiles.from: Donovan, Bombay
subfiles.about: Reports a Times of India article disputing claims of starvation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Bombay telegram summarizing Noyes Thomas's Tokyo despatch that Japan had no starvation and hid food stocks, and Admiral Fraser's statement that he saw none.

subfiles.title: Church World Service Inquiry About Sending Relief Funds to Japan
subfiles.from: A. Henry Birkel, Church World Service
subfiles.to: Paul F. McGuire, Department of State
subfiles.about: Asks whether funds can be remitted to G. Ernest Bott in Tokyo for relief work.
subfiles.summary: Church World Service, merged from three Protestant bodies, explains Fred Moore is no longer involved; G. Ernest Bott requested funds in Tokyo, prompting a renewed inquiry on financial rules for private relief in Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply on Procedures for Relief-Fund Remittances
subfiles.from: Paul F. McGuire, Department of State
subfiles.to: A. Henry Birkel, Church World Service
subfiles.about: Reports that procedures for moderate relief remittances to Japan should become effective within a month.
subfiles.summary: McGuire says procedures are being devised to make moderate transfers for relief unobjectionable and asks Church World Service to estimate monthly or annual remittances.

subfiles.title: Congressman Havenner's Inquiry About Relief for a Kobe Orphanage
subfiles.from: Franck R. Havenner
subfiles.about: Requests guidance in answering an inquiry about sending food, clothing, and medicine to a Kobe orphanage.
subfiles.summary: Congressman Havenner quotes Presbyterian missions official Gordon Chapman asking when private relief may go to Japan, especially for a Kobe orphanage of bombing orphans, and asks how to reply.

subfiles.title: Reply to Congressman Havenner Identifying LARA as the Relief Channel
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains that LARA is the accredited channel for private relief shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: State tells Havenner approved agencies may send supplies distributed by need, Church World Service already shipped, and the Council's member agencies formed LARA, whose representatives are going to Japan; Chapman should contact LARA about the Kobe orphanage.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Social-Welfare Materials and a Possible Welfare Commission
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Records discussions with Colonel Nelson B. Neff about educational materials and long-term social-welfare policy for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Neff describes Japan's need for social-work literature, training aids and a lasting welfare program; participants agree the War Department should coordinate materials with State, the Federal Security Agency and professional groups; a December 12 addendum says the War Department found materials, and Neff hopes to explore a welfare commission.

subfiles.title: Request for Social-Work Literature and Training Aids
subfiles.from: Crawford F. Sams, SCAP Public Health and Welfare Section
subfiles.to: Otis E. Mulliken, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests educational materials to support social-work training and public assistance in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Sams says Japan's public-assistance program for millions under the Daily Life Security Law lacks trained social workers; he requests literature on casework, public welfare, insurance, child welfare and curricula, as SCAP supervises training seen as strengthening democracy.

subfiles.title: Reply to Crawford Sams on Social-Welfare Assistance
subfiles.from: Otis E. Mulliken, Department of State
subfiles.about: Promises coordinated assistance in obtaining materials for Japan's social-work education program.
subfiles.summary: Mulliken reports that Department officers had discussed the immediate and long-range welfare problems with Nelson B. Neff. The State Department intended to cooperate with the War Department, other federal bodies, voluntary agencies, and professional organizations. He assures Sams of continued interest and welcomes further suggestions.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Approved SWNCC Food Policy Paper
subfiles.from: State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Forwards the approved and amended SWNCC 331/3 food-policy paper for action in the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: The Committee approved SWNCC 331/3 on February 19, amended to call it substantially the 1945 U.S. policy sent to SCAP, and asks State to send a copy to the U.S. Far Eastern Commission member.

subfiles.title: Decision Amending SWNCC 331/3
subfiles.from: Secretariat, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Directs holders to replace a page in the food-policy paper with a revised version.
subfiles.summary: The duplicate copies record the Committee's February 19 approval and amendment of SWNCC 331/3. Holders are instructed to substitute revised page 22 and destroy the superseded page by burning.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 331/3: Food Policy for Japan
subfiles.from: State member and Secretariat, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Develops a U.S. negotiating position on Far Eastern Commission policy for civilian food relief in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The study analyzes proposed Far Eastern Commission revisions to U.S. food policy, balancing protection of SCAP's authority against Allied concern that Japan not receive preferential access during the world food shortage. It recommends emphasizing Japanese self-help, equitable distribution, maximum domestic production, suppression of black markets and nonfood diversion, and only minimum reliance on imports. Imported food would be justified chiefly to prevent disease or unrest threatening occupation objectives or forces, while no preference should be granted over Allied or liberated populations. The appendix sets out the proposed policy and a U.S. statement defining how SCAP would report needs and how Washington would determine permissible import levels.

subfiles.title: Instructions to the U.S. Member of the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.from: Ernest A. Gross for J. H. Hilldring, Department of State
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Authorizes negotiations on Japanese food policy using the approved SWNCC 331/3 position.
subfiles.summary: Memo encloses SWNCC 331/3 with its amended introduction and authorizes the U.S. Far Eastern Commission member to negotiate on its conclusions.

subfiles.title: Clara Neely's Inquiry About Gift Parcels to Japan
subfiles.from: Clara J. Neely
subfiles.about: Requests information about sending small bags of food, clothing, and other articles to suffering people in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Clara Neely asks about collecting and mailing small relief parcels for Japanese lacking food and clothing, especially missionaries and orphans, and whether heavy duties apply.

subfiles.title: Reply to Clara Neely on Japanese Gift-Parcel Tariffs
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Department of State
subfiles.about: States that Japan does not levy a tariff on gift-parcel contents and encloses the relevant postal regulation.
subfiles.summary: Martin tells Neely Japan imposed no tariffs on gift-parcel contents, enclosing the U.S. postal regulation defining gift parcels.

subfiles.title: Letter to John Taber on Japanese Liquid Assets and Food Imports
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains why Japanese liquid assets should support economic revival rather than be exhausted on food imports.
subfiles.summary: Letter to John Taber divides Japanese liquid assets into identifiable looted, unidentifiable looted and legitimate, totaling $275-300 million per MacArthur; the Department argues using nonrestitutable assets for raw materials to revive exports would make Japan self-supporting and protect taxpayers better than spending them solely on food.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Statements on Foreign Relief and Japanese Assets
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Sends two statements answering congressional questions about foreign relief and Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: Acheson sends Taber statements on foreign-relief programs and using Japanese liquid assets for food, offering more information and an informal discussion with his subcommittee.

subfiles.title: Foreign Relief Programs
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Summarizes U.S. foreign-relief appropriations, expenditures, programs, and country allocations.
subfiles.summary: Foreign Relief Programs: fiscal 1947 and 1948 relief estimated at $3.447 billion for post-UNRRA, occupied-country and refugee programs; Greek and Turkish aid distinguished; the War Department's $1.025 billion request is allocated among Germany, Austria, Japan including the Ryukyus, and Korea, with $415 million for Japan.

subfiles.title: Use of Japanese Liquid Assets to Purchase Food
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Argues for using nonrestitutable Japanese assets to revive productive industry instead of financing food alone.
subfiles.summary: Statement classing Japanese liquid assets as looted and identifiable, looted but unidentifiable, or legitimate, citing MacArthur's valuation and the Far Eastern Commission's role; the Department favors using them for raw materials and export recovery so Japan becomes self-sustaining, not for food.

subfiles.title: Buenos Aires Inquiry About Japanese Relief Shipments
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Asks whether local Japanese may send food or clothing to Japan and Okinawa and through which agencies.
subfiles.summary: Buenos Aires asks instructions for the local Japanese community: whether supplies may go directly or through the U.S. and which agencies to use.

subfiles.title: Airgram to Santiago Identifying LARA as the Approved Relief Agency
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Advises that the Chilean Red Cross should coordinate its proposed Japan shipment through LARA.
subfiles.summary: Airgram: LARA is the only agency SCAP recognizes to receive and distribute relief in Japan; Chile's Red Cross should contact LARA chairman Edward Peacock, with distribution jointly by LARA and Japanese agencies under U.S. military supervision.

subfiles.title: Reply to Buenos Aires on Parcels and Bulk Relief
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Directs Argentine donors to postal authorities for parcels and to LARA for bulk relief shipments.
subfiles.summary: State tells Buenos Aires to consult the Argentine Post Office on Japan gift parcels, direct bulk-shipment questions to LARA chairman Edward Peacock, and notes mail arrangements weren't complete.

subfiles.title: Internal Note on Argentine Relief and Parcel-Post Arrangements
subfiles.from: Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Records War and Post Office Department advice on proposed Argentine shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Colonel Linville says Argentina's Japanese group should ask LARA whether it accepts supplies and the War Department doesn't object; Mr. Peterson says parcel post could pass through the U.S. if Argentina packs parcels into bulk containers.

subfiles.title: Request for Recommendation on Supplies for the Sacred Heart Convent
subfiles.from: War Department Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Requests a recommendation on a proposed shipment of equipment, bedding, and food to a Tokyo convent.
subfiles.summary: War Department message: a Pacific trading company wants to send Reverend Mother Britt of the Sacred Heart Convent in Tokyo blankets, mattresses, trunks, a typewriter and about 1.5 tons of food; theater authorities are asked for a recommendation.

subfiles.title: Buenos Aires Follow-up on Bulk Relief for the Ryukyu Islands
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Asks whether bulk relief may now be sent to the Ryukyu Islands under the same rules as shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Buenos Aires cites earlier Japanese and Okinawan relief correspondence and the restored Ryukyu postal and gift-parcel service, asking whether bulk shipments are also allowed and whether Japan's regulations and mails apply.

subfiles.title: Reply Authorizing Bulk Relief Through LARA
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Advises that bulk relief shipments may be made through LARA.
subfiles.summary: State confirms bulk relief may go through LARA; shippers should contact Edward Peacock for regulations.

subfiles.title: Chilean Red Cross Inquiry About Relief for Japanese Children
subfiles.from: Claude G. Bowers, U.S. Embassy, Santiago
subfiles.about: Asks how a Chilean Japanese community may send food and clothing to needy children in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Chilean Red Cross was asked to send 100,000 pesos of clothing and food to the Japanese Red Cross for children, with Grace Line offering transport to San Francisco; the Embassy asks whether onward shipment is allowed and what U.S. authorizations are needed.

subfiles.title: Chinese Red Cross Medical Supplies for Shikoku Earthquake Victims
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports the transfer of Chinese-donated medical supplies to Japanese victims of the December 1946 Shikoku earthquake.
subfiles.summary: The Chinese Mission gave about thirty cases of Chinese Red Cross medical supplies for Shikoku earthquake victims, transferred August 27 via SCAP welfare and Red Cross representatives; many cases bore U.S. Medical, UNRRA, CNRA or American Red Cross markings, worth $4,000-$5,000, and officials questioned diverting supplies needed in China.

subfiles.title: Confidential Transmittal of the Earthquake-Relief Despatch
subfiles.from: William H. McCahon, Department of State
subfiles.to: Philip E. Ryan, American Red Cross
subfiles.about: Confidentially forwards the Tokyo despatch on Chinese Red Cross aid to Japanese earthquake victims.
subfiles.summary: McCahon confidentially sends Ryan despatch 1268 from the Tokyo Political Adviser on the Chinese Red Cross contribution for Shikoku earthquake victims.

subfiles.title: American Red Cross Acknowledgment and Supply Investigation
subfiles.from: Philip E. Ryan, American Red Cross
subfiles.to: William H. McCahon, Department of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the earthquake-relief report and notes an investigation into the supplies' source.
subfiles.summary: Ryan says American Red Cross representatives in Tokyo already reported the Chinese contribution, and its Shanghai representative is investigating the supplies' original source.

subfiles.title: Argentine Diplomatic Note on a 52-Ton Relief Shipment
subfiles.doc_type: diplomatic note with English translation and Spanish original
subfiles.from: Oscar Ivanissevich, Argentine Ambassador
subfiles.to: Robert E. Lovett, U.S. Under Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests assistance forwarding an Argentine government gift of provisions to Japan and Okinawa through LARA.
subfiles.summary: Argentina's aid committee shipped 52 tons of provisions on the Fisk Victory October 14, a gift from President Peron to Japan and Okinawa via San Francisco; bills of lading went to the consul for LARA, and the Ambassador asks U.S. authorities to expedite reshipment.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of the Argentine Relief Shipment
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Confirms that arrangements were made to forward Argentina's relief supplies to Japan and Okinawa.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Argentine note D.E. 518 on the gift routed through LARA and says forwarding arrangements are complete.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Arrangements for the Argentine Shipment
subfiles.from: Mrs. Correll, Department of State
subfiles.about: Records confirmation that LARA had already arranged to handle the Argentine relief shipment.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Correll contacted the Advisory Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid about Argentina's October 28 note; Miss Borschke consulted LARA, which was already coordinating with the Embassy.
